Intermediate model: int_marketing__campaigns_cleaned

Source: Salesforce Campaigns Object

Cleaned campaign data for marketing attribution and ROI analysis.

IMPORTANT:
- Campaign hierarchies in SFDC are complex (parent/child relationships)
- campaign_member data is in separate model (int_marketing__campaign_members)
- UTM mapping happens downstream in fct_marketing_attribution

- Finance (2024-08-01): "Need campaign costs for marketing ROI report"
- Marcus (2024-08-01): "Garbage in, garbage out. Talk to Marketing."

    SELECT * FROM {{ ref('stg_sfdc__campaigns') }}

),

cleaned AS (

    SELECT
        _id,
        _loaded_at,
        _source_system,
        _source_table,
        _row_hash,

        -- Data quality flags
        TRUE AS _is_valid,
        FALSE AS _has_nulls,
        CURRENT_TIMESTAMP AS _cleaned_at

    FROM source
    WHERE 1=1  -- Add filters as needed

),

deduplicated AS (

    SELECT DISTINCT *
    FROM cleaned

)

/*
================================================================================
Campaign Daily Performance Fact

@author: Marketing Analytics Team (Amy Chen)
@created: 2023-09-10
@modified: 2024-11-05 - Added conversion rate calculation

Daily aggregation of campaign metrics from all marketing channels.
Used by marketing dashboards and budget allocation models.

Performance: Full refresh 4 min, ~2M rows
Schedule: Daily at 5 AM UTC (after marketing data lands at 3 AM)

KNOWN ISSUES:
- Facebook data delayed 24hrs, so yesterday's metrics incomplete until day+2
- Google Ads attribution window = 30d, causes late conversions
- TikTok integration broken since 2024-10-15 (DATA-1892)

TODO: Add cost-per-acquisition calculation
TODO: Add ROAS (return on ad spend) metric
TODO: Handle attribution window properly for accurate conversion counts
FIXME: conversion_rate_pct is misleading - it's click-to-conversion not impression
HACK: Using nullif to avoid div-by-zero but masks data quality issues
================================================================================
*/

with campaign_performance as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_marketing__campaign_performance') }}
    -- FIXME: Filter out test campaigns that marketing forgot to exclude
),

marketing_campaigns as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_marketing__marketing_campaigns') }}
)

select
    cp.metric_date,
    mc.campaign_name,
    mc.campaign_type,
    cp.impressions,
    cp.clicks,
    cp.conversions,
    cp.spend,
    cp.revenue,
    round(100.0 * cp.clicks / nullif(cp.impressions, 0), 2) as ctr_pct,
    round(100.0 * cp.conversions / nullif(cp.clicks, 0), 2) as conversion_rate_pct
from campaign_performance cp
left join marketing_campaigns mc on cp.campaign_id = mc.campaign_id
order by 1, 2

{#
    @author: Jennifer Martinez (Revenue Operations)
    @created: 2022-09-12
    @modified: 2024-10-03 by Ahmed Hassan

    == Promotion Profitability Analysis ==

    Tracks coupon/promo code performance to help Finance understand
    the true cost of our promotions. CFO requested this after Q2 2022
    when we realized some "successful" promos actually lost money.

    BUSINESS CONTEXT:
    - Marketing creates promos in Salesforce
    - Customers redeem via POS or web checkout
    - This model reconciles redemptions with order revenue
    - Finance uses this for monthly close + margin analysis

    == Source Data ==
    - stg_marketing__coupon_redemptions: POS/web redemption events
    - stg_orders__orders: Order totals (grand_total includes tax, excludes shipping)
    - stg_marketing__coupons: Coupon master data from SFDC

    == Known Issues ==
    1. discount_amount doesn't account for "stackable" promos - DATA-1023
       When customers use multiple codes, we double-count the discount. Finance
       hates this but fixing it requires POS changes. Estimated 8% error rate.

    2. grand_total in orders includes tax but discount_amount is pre-tax.
       We're comparing apples to oranges. Ahmed tried to fix this in Oct 2024
       but it broke month-end reconciliation so we reverted. (DATA-1567)

    3. ~5% of redemptions don't match to orders due to timing issues.
       POS sends redemption event before order completes. Usually resolves
       in T+1 but monthly reports can be off. (DATA-789)

/*
================================================================================
Campaign Daily Performance Fact

@author: Marketing Analytics Team (Amy Chen)
@created: 2023-09-10
@modified: 2024-11-05 - Added conversion rate calculation

Daily aggregation of campaign metrics from all marketing channels.
Used by marketing dashboards and budget allocation models.

Performance: Full refresh 4 min, ~2M rows
Schedule: Daily at 5 AM UTC (after marketing data lands at 3 AM)

KNOWN ISSUES:
- Facebook data delayed 24hrs, so yesterday's metrics incomplete until day+2
- Google Ads attribution window = 30d, causes late conversions
- TikTok integration broken since 2024-10-15 (DATA-1892)

TODO: Add cost-per-acquisition calculation
TODO: Add ROAS (return on ad spend) metric
TODO: Handle attribution window properly for accurate conversion counts
FIXME: conversion_rate_pct is misleading - it's click-to-conversion not impression
HACK: Using nullif to avoid div-by-zero but masks data quality issues
================================================================================
*/

with campaign_performance as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_marketing__campaign_performance') }}
    -- FIXME: Filter out test campaigns that marketing forgot to exclude
),

marketing_campaigns as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_marketing__marketing_campaigns') }}
)

select
    cp.metric_date,
    mc.campaign_name,
    mc.campaign_type,
    cp.impressions,
    cp.clicks,
    cp.conversions,
    cp.spend,
    cp.revenue,
    round(100.0 * cp.clicks / nullif(cp.impressions, 0), 2) as ctr_pct,
    round(100.0 * cp.conversions / nullif(cp.clicks, 0), 2) as conversion_rate_pct
from campaign_performance cp
left join marketing_campaigns mc on cp.campaign_id = mc.campaign_id
order by 1, 2

        tags=['marketing', 'promotions', 'finance_reporting'],

    )
}}

{#
    @author: Jennifer Martinez (Revenue Operations)
    @created: 2022-09-12
    @modified: 2024-10-03 by Ahmed Hassan

    == Promotion Profitability Analysis ==

    Tracks coupon/promo code performance to help Finance understand
    the true cost of our promotions. CFO requested this after Q2 2022
    when we realized some "successful" promos actually lost money.

    BUSINESS CONTEXT:
    - Marketing creates promos in Salesforce
    - Customers redeem via POS or web checkout
    - This model reconciles redemptions with order revenue
    - Finance uses this for monthly close + margin analysis

    == Source Data ==
    - stg_marketing__coupon_redemptions: POS/web redemption events
    - stg_orders__orders: Order totals (grand_total includes tax, excludes shipping)
    - stg_marketing__coupons: Coupon master data from SFDC

    == Known Issues ==
    1. discount_amount doesn't account for "stackable" promos - DATA-1023
       When customers use multiple codes, we double-count the discount. Finance
       hates this but fixing it requires POS changes. Estimated 8% error rate.

    2. grand_total in orders includes tax but discount_amount is pre-tax.
       We're comparing apples to oranges. Ahmed tried to fix this in Oct 2024
       but it broke month-end reconciliation so we reverted. (DATA-1567)

    3. ~5% of redemptions don't match to orders due to timing issues.
       POS sends redemption event before order completes. Usually resolves
       in T+1 but monthly reports can be off. (DATA-789)

### Task: Fix CAC Payback Waterfall

You're an analytics engineer rebuilding a **CAC payback waterfall** report. The warehouse already contains a reference dbt project at `/app/dbt_transforms` with various models materialized. Marketing spend data exists in the warehouse -- find the right source table by exploring available models.

Create a dbt project at `/app/dbt_project` and implement:
- `models/marts/marketing/rpt_cac_payback_waterfall_fixed.sql`

## Database Backend

This task supports two database backends:

- **DuckDB**: Local DuckDB database at `/app/database/retail.duckdb`. The dbt project is at `/app/dbt_models_duckdb/`.
- **Snowflake**: Cloud Snowflake database. Connection details are provided via environment variables (`SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT`, `SNOWFLAKE_USER`, `SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD`, `SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE`, `SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA`, `SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE`, `SNOWFLAKE_ROLE`). The dbt project is at `/app/dbt_models_snowflake/`.

Check the `DB_TYPE` environment variable to determine which 
[EXCERPT OMISSION]
l per **campaign_id** (grain: one row per `campaign_id` + `days_since_cohort`).
- **Channel key handling**: Each campaign must have exactly one `channel_key` in the output. If the source data has a campaign appearing across multiple `channel_key` values, pick the `channel_key` with the highest total `spend_amount` for that campaign. Aggregate all spend and revenue across channel keys into a single campaign row before building the waterfall.
- Include all campaign-days in the data and compute daily and cumulative values.
- Round currency fields to 2 decimals and payback_ratio to 4 decimals.

#### Quality requirements
- No negative spends or revenue.
- `cumulative_spend` and `cumulative_revenue` must be non-decreasing within each campaign.
- Reconciliation: for each campaign, the last row's cumulative totals must equal total source values within 0.01.

# Daily Cohorts Reporting

Build a dbt model called `rpt_daily_cohorts` that analyzes customer retention by grouping customers into cohorts based on when they first placed an order.

## Database Backend

This task supports both DuckDB and Snowflake. **Run `echo $DB_TYPE` in a shell BEFORE you write any code or spawn any subagents — the live env determines which backend the verifier runs against.** Do NOT assume a default from this prose. Both `/app/dbt_models_duckdb/` and `/app/dbt_models_snowflake/` exist on disk; the verifier only checks the project matching the live `$DB_TYPE`.

### DuckDB
- Set `DB_TYPE=duckdb`
- Database path: `$DUCKDB_PATH` (default: `/app/database/retail.duckdb`)

### Snowflake
- Set `DB_TYPE=snowflake`
- Environment variables (pre-configured):
  - `SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_USER`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE` - The clone database to use
  - `SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_ROLE` (optional)

{{
    config(
        materialized='view',
        tags=['time_series', 'sales', 'monthly', 'channel']
    )
}}

/*
 * Time Series: Channel Revenue & Margin - Monthly
 * Aggregates sales revenue, profit, and margin metrics by channel per month
 */

with sales_data as (
    select
        d.date_key,
        d.full_date,
        d.month_number,
        d.year,
        f.channel_key,
        f.order_id,
        s.total_amount,
        s.profit_amount,
        s.discount_amount
    from {{ ref('dim_fact_sales') }} f
    join {{ ref('stg_fact_sales') }} s
        on f.sales_id = s.sale_key
    join {{ ref('stg_analytics__dim_date') }} d
        on f.date_key = d.date_key
    where f.sales_id is not null
      and f.channel_key is not null
),

monthly_channel_agg as (
    select
        date_trunc('month', sales_data.full_date) as month_start,
        sales_data.year as sales_year,
        sales_data.month_number as sales_month,
        cast(sales_data.channel_key as text) as channel_key,
        c.channel_id,
        c.channel_code,
        c.channel_name,
        c.channel_type,
        count(distinct sales_data.order_id) as order_count,
        sum(sales_data.total_amount) as revenue,
        sum(sales_data.profit_amount) as profit,
        sum(sales_data.discount_amount) as discount_amount,
        current_timestamp as dbt_updated_at
    from sales_data
    join {{ ref('dim_dim_channel') }} c
        on cast(sales_data.channel_key as text) = c.channel_id
    group by
        date_trunc('month', sales_data.full_date),
        sales_data.year,
        sales_data.month_number,
        sales_data.channel_key,
        c.channel_id,
        c.channel_code,
        c.channel_name,
        c.channel_type
)

select
    month_start,
    sales_year,
    sales_month,
    channel_key,
    channel_id,
    channel_code,
    channel_name,
    channel_type,
    order_count,
    revenue,
    profit,
    discount_amount,
    nullif(profit, 0) / nullif(revenue, 0) as margin_rate,
    nullif(revenue, 0) / nullif(order_count, 0) as avg_order_value,
    nullif(discount_amount, 0) / nullif(revenue + discount_amount, 0) as discount_rate,
    dbt_updated_at
from monthly_channel_agg
order by month_start, channel_key
EOF
",
      "duration": 0.5
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "dbt run --select ts_sales__channel_revenue_margin_monthly 2>&1
",

    }
  ]

## Goal
Create a dbt model that outputs monthly `revenue`,`profit`,`discount_amount`,`margin_rate`,`avg_order_value`,`discount_rate` by channel. The result should support channel mix and budget optimization analysis.

## Database Backend

This task supports both DuckDB and Snowflake. **Run `echo $DB_TYPE` in a shell BEFORE you write any code or spawn any subagents — the live env determines which backend the verifier runs against.** Do NOT assume a default from this prose. Both `/app/dbt_models_duckdb/` and `/app/dbt_models_snowflake/` exist on disk; the verifier only checks the project matching the live `$DB_TYPE`.

### DuckDB
- Set `DB_TYPE=duckdb`
- Database path: `$DUCKDB_PATH` (default: `/app/database/retail.duckdb`)
- Model location: `/app/dbt_models_duckdb/models/marts/time_series/sales/ts_sales__channel_revenue_margin_monthly.sql`

### Snowflake
- Set `DB_TYPE=snowflake`
- Environment variables (pre-configured):

task_requirement_excerpt.text:
# Daily Order Summary

The operations team needs a daily view of order activity to plan staffing and logistics. They want to track order volume and revenue trends over time, excluding cancelled or failed orders.

## Your Task

Create a **standalone dbt project** at `/app/dbt_project` with a model called `daily_order_summary` that aggregates orders by date.

**Important**: Do NOT use the existing dbt project directories. Create a fresh dbt project from scratch.

## Database Backend

This task supports both DuckDB and Snowflake. **Run `echo $DB_TYPE` in a shell BEFORE you write any code or spawn any subagents — the live env determines which backend the verifier runs against.** Do NOT assume a default from this prose. Reference dbt projects exist at `/app/dbt_models_duckdb/` and `/app/dbt_models_snowflake/` for inspection only. Write your dbt project at `/app/dbt_project` — outputs in the reference directories are not graded.

### DuckDB
- Set `DB_TYPE=duckdb`
- Database path: `$DUCKDB_PA
[EXCERPT OMISSION]
 the `ORDERS.ORDERS` table which contains order records with columns including:
- `ORDERED_AT` - timestamp when order was placed
- `GRAND_TOTAL` - order total amount
- `STATUS` - order status (e.g., 'COMPLETED', 'SHIPPED', 'CANCELLED', 'RETURNED', 'FAILED')

## Requirements

1. Extract the date from `ORDERED_AT` timestamp
2. Exclude orders with STATUS IN ('CANCELLED', 'RETURNED', 'FAILED')
3. Group by order date and calculate:
   - Count of orders
   - Sum of revenue (rounded to 2 decimal places)
4. Sort results by order_date ascending

## Output Model

Create a model named `daily_order_summary` in schema `daily_analytics` with these columns:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| order_date | The date (not timestamp) of orders |
| order_count | Number of orders placed that day |
| total_revenue | Sum of GRAND_TOTAL, rounded to 2 decimals |

## Technical Notes

- Configure the schema in `profiles.yml`, not in `dbt_project.yml`
- The model should be materialized as a table

task_requirement_excerpt.text:
### Task: Fix CAC Payback Waterfall

You're an analytics engineer rebuilding a **CAC payback waterfall** report. The warehouse already contains a reference dbt project at `/app/dbt_transforms` with various models materialized. Marketing spend data exists in the warehouse -- find the right source table by exploring available models.

Create a dbt project at `/app/dbt_project` and implement:
- `models/marts/marketing/rpt_cac_payback_waterfall_fixed.sql`

## Database Backend

This task supports two database backends:

- **DuckDB**: Local DuckDB database at `/app/database/retail.duckdb`. The dbt project is at `/app/dbt_models_duckdb/`.
- **Snowflake**: Cloud Snowflake database. Connection details are provided via environment variables (`SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT`, `SNOWFLAKE_USER`, `SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD`, `SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE`, `SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA`, `SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE`, `SNOWFLAKE_ROLE`). The dbt project is at `/app/dbt_models_snowflake/`.

Check the `DB_TYPE` environment variable to determine which 
[EXCERPT OMISSION]
l per **campaign_id** (grain: one row per `campaign_id` + `days_since_cohort`).
- **Channel key handling**: Each campaign must have exactly one `channel_key` in the output. If the source data has a campaign appearing across multiple `channel_key` values, pick the `channel_key` with the highest total `spend_amount` for that campaign. Aggregate all spend and revenue across channel keys into a single campaign row before building the waterfall.
- Include all campaign-days in the data and compute daily and cumulative values.
- Round currency fields to 2 decimals and payback_ratio to 4 decimals.

#### Quality requirements
- No negative spends or revenue.
- `cumulative_spend` and `cumulative_revenue` must be non-decreasing within each campaign.
- Reconciliation: for each campaign, the last row's cumulative totals must equal total source values within 0.01.

#### Environment notes
- Base image includes dbt + DuckDB + `/app/dbt_transforms`.
- Your dbt profile should write to schema `analytics`.

task_requirement_excerpt.text:
# Daily Order Summary

The operations team needs a daily view of order activity to plan staffing and logistics. They want to track order volume and revenue trends over time, excluding cancelled or failed orders.

## Your Task

Create a **standalone dbt project** at `/app/dbt_project` with a model called `daily_order_summary` that aggregates orders by date.

**Important**: Do NOT use the existing dbt project directories. Create a fresh dbt project from scratch.

## Database Backend

This task supports both DuckDB and Snowflake. **Run `echo $DB_TYPE` in a shell BEFORE you write any code or spawn any subagents — the live env determines which backend the verifier runs against.** Do NOT assume a default from this prose. Reference dbt projects exist at `/app/dbt_models_duckdb/` and `/app/dbt_models_snowflake/` for inspection only. Write your dbt project at `/app/dbt_project` — outputs in the reference directories are not graded.

### DuckDB
- Set `DB_TYPE=duckdb`
- Database path: `$DUCKDB_PA
[EXCERPT OMISSION]
 the `ORDERS.ORDERS` table which contains order records with columns including:
- `ORDERED_AT` - timestamp when order was placed
- `GRAND_TOTAL` - order total amount
- `STATUS` - order status (e.g., 'COMPLETED', 'SHIPPED', 'CANCELLED', 'RETURNED', 'FAILED')

## Requirements

1. Extract the date from `ORDERED_AT` timestamp
2. Exclude orders with STATUS IN ('CANCELLED', 'RETURNED', 'FAILED')
3. Group by order date and calculate:
   - Count of orders
   - Sum of revenue (rounded to 2 decimal places)
4. Sort results by order_date ascending

## Output Model

Create a model named `daily_order_summary` in schema `daily_analytics` with these columns:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| order_date | The date (not timestamp) of orders |
| order_count | Number of orders placed that day |
| total_revenue | Sum of GRAND_TOTAL, rounded to 2 decimals |

## Technical Notes

- Configure the schema in `profiles.yml`, not in `dbt_project.yml`
- The model should be materialized as a table

/*
 * Time Series: Channel Revenue and Margin - Monthly
 * Aggregates sales metrics by channel and month for budget optimization analysis
 */

with sales_data as (
    select
        -- Date fields from date dimension
        d.full_date,
        d.year as sales_year,
        d.month_number as sales_month,
        date_trunc('month', d.full_date) as month_start,
        
        -- Channel fields (cast channel_key to text for join)
        cast(df.channel_key as text) as channel_key,
        df.channel_id,
        df.channel_code,
        df.channel_name,
        df.channel_type,
        
        -- Order identifier
        df.order_id,
        
        -- Monetary metrics from sales fact
        s.total_amount,
        s.profit_amount as profit,
        s.discount_amount
    from {{ ref('stg_analytics__dim_date') }} d
    inner join {{ ref('dim_fact_sales') }} df
        on d.date_key = df.date_key
    inner join {{ ref('stg_fact_sales') }} s
        on df.sales_key = s.sale_key
    where d.full_date is not null
      and df.channel_key is not null
),

aggregated as (
    select
        month_start,
        sales_year,
        sales_month,
        channel_key,
        channel_id,
        channel_code,
        channel_name,
        channel_type,
        
        -- Order count (distinct orders per channel per month)
        count(distinct order_id) as order_count,
        
        -- Revenue: sum of total sales amount
        sum(total_amount) as revenue,
        
        -- Profit: sum of profit amount
        sum(profit) as profit,
        
        -- Discount amount: sum of discount
        sum(discount_amount) as discount_amount,
        
        -- Margin rate: profit / revenue (safe division with nullif)
        nullif(sum(profit), 0) * 1.0 / nullif(sum(total_amount), 0) as margin_rate,
        
        -- Avg order value: revenue / distinct order count
        sum(total_amount) * 1.0 / count(distinct order_id) as avg_order_value,
        
        -- Discount rate: discount / (total + discount)
        nullif(sum(discount_amount), 0) * 1.0 / nullif(sum(total_amount) + sum(discount_amount), 0) as discount_rate,
        
        -- Timestamp
        current_timestamp as dbt_updated_at
    
    from sales_data
    group by month_start, sales_year, sales_month, channel_key, channel_id, channel_code, channel_name, channel_type
)

select *
from aggregated
order by month_start, channel_key

cat > models/marts/analytics/rpt_daily_cohorts.sql << 'EOF'
-- Daily Cohorts Retention Analysis
-- Groups customers by their first order date and tracks retention over time

with
-- Get the first order date for each customer (their cohort date)
first_orders as (
    select
        customer_id,
        date_trunc('day', ordered_at) as cohort_date
    from {{ source('orders', 'ORDERS') }}
    where customer_id is not null
    group by customer_id, date_trunc('day', ordered_at)
),

-- Get all orders with cohort date attached
orders_with_cohort as (
    select
        o.customer_id,
        date_trunc('day', o.ordered_at) as order_date,
        fo.cohort_date,
        (o.ordered_at - fo.cohort_date) as days_since_cohort
    from {{ source('orders', 'ORDERS') }} o
    join first_orders fo on o.customer_id = fo.customer_id
    where o.customer_id is not null
),

-- Calculate cumulative customers for each cohort at each time bucket
cohort_customers as (
    select
        cohort_date,
        days_since_cohort,
        count(distinct customer_id) as customer_count
    from orders_with_cohort
    group by cohort_date, days_since_cohort
),

-- Get unique cohort dates and their sizes
cohort_sizes as (
    select
        cohort_date,
        count(distinct customer_id) as cohort_size
    from first_orders
    group by cohort_date
),

-- Calculate cumulative counts for each day bucket
cohort_daily_counts as (
    select
        cs.cohort_date,
        cs.cohort_size,
        coalesce(sum(case when cc.days_since_cohort = 0 then cc.customer_count else 0 end), 0) as day_0_customers,
        coalesce(sum(case when cc.days_since_cohort <= 7 then cc.customer_count else 0 end), 0) as day_7_customers,
        coalesce(sum(case when cc.days_since_cohort <= 30 then cc.customer_count else 0 end), 0) as day_30_customers,
        coalesce(sum(case when cc.days_since_cohort <= 90 then cc.customer_count else 0 end), 0) as day_90_customers
    from cohort_sizes cs
    left join cohort_customers cc on cs.cohort_date = cc.cohort_date
    group by cs.cohort_date, cs.cohort_size
),

-- Calculate retention rates
final as (
    select
        cohort_date,
        cohort_size,
        day_0_customers,
        day_7_customers,
        day_30_customers,
        day_90_customers,
        round(day_0_customers * 1.0 / nullif(cohort_size, 0), 4) as day_0_retention,
        round(day_7_customers * 1.0 / nullif(cohort_size, 0), 4) as day_7_retention,
        round(day_30_customers * 1.0 / nullif(cohort_size, 0), 4) as day_30_retention,
        round(day_90_customers * 1.0 / nullif(cohort_size, 0), 4) as day_90_retention
    from cohort_daily_counts
)

select
    cohort_date,
    cohort_size,
    day_0_customers,
    day_7_customers,
    day_30_customers,
    day_90_customers,
    day_0_retention,
    day_7_retention,
    day_30_retention,
    day_90_retention
from final
order by cohort_date
EOF

        -- Date fields from date dimension
        d.full_date,
        d.year as sales_year,
        d.month_number as sales_month,
        date_trunc('month', d.full_date) as month_start,

    inner join {{ ref('dim_dim_channel') }} dc

    where d.full_date is not null

),

        sales_year,
        sales_month,
        channel_key,
        channel_id,
        channel_code,
        channel_name,
        channel_type,
        
        -- Order count (distinct orders per channel per month)
        count(distinct order_id) as order_count,
        
        -- Revenue: sum of total sales amount
        sum(total_amount) as revenue,
        
        -- Profit: sum of profit amount
        sum(profit) as profit,
        
        -- Discount amount: sum of discount
        sum(discount_amount) as discount_amount,
        
        -- Margin rate: profit / revenue (safe division with nullif)
        nullif(sum(profit), 0) * 1.0 / nullif(sum(total_amount), 0) as margin_rate,
        
        -- Avg order value: revenue / distinct order count
        sum(total_amount) * 1.0 / count(distinct order_id) as avg_order_value,
        
        -- Discount rate: discount / (total + discount)
        nullif(sum(discount_amount), 0) * 1.0 / nullif(sum(total_amount) + sum(discount_amount), 0) as discount_rate,
        
        -- Timestamp
        current_timestamp as dbt_updated_at

## Metric definitions

-- Daily Cohorts Retention Analysis
-- Groups customers by their first order date and tracks retention over time

with
-- Get the first order date for each customer (their cohort date)
first_orders as (
    select
        customer_id,
        date_trunc('day', ordered_at) as cohort_date
    from {{ source('orders', 'ORDERS') }}
    where customer_id is not null
    group by customer_id, date_trunc('day', ordered_at)
),

-- Get all orders with cohort date attached
orders_with_cohort as (
    select
        o.customer_id,
        date_trunc('day', o.ordered_at) as order_date,
        fo.cohort_date,
        cast((o.ordered_at - fo.cohort_date) as int) as days_since_cohort
    from {{ source('orders', 'ORDERS') }} o
    join first_orders fo on o.customer_id = fo.customer_id
    where o.customer_id is not null
),

-- Calculate cumulative customers for each cohort at each time bucket
cohort_customers as (
    select
        cohort_date,
        days_since_cohort,
        count(distinct customer_id) as customer_count
    from orders_with_cohort
    group by cohort_date, days_since_cohort
),

-- Get unique cohort dates and their sizes
cohort_sizes as (
    select
        cohort_date,
        count(distinct customer_id) as cohort_size
    from first_orders
    group by cohort_date
),

-- Calculate cumulative counts for each day bucket
cohort_daily_counts as (
    select
        cs.cohort_date,
        cs.cohort_size,
        coalesce(sum(case when cc.days_since_cohort = 0 then cc.customer_count else 0 end), 0) as day_0_customers,

    from cohort_sizes cs
    left join cohort_customers cc on cs.cohort_date = cc.cohort_date
    group by cs.cohort_date, cs.cohort_size
),

-- Calculate retention rates
final as (
    select
        cohort_date,
        cohort_size,
        day_0_customers,
        day_7_customers,
        day_30_customers,
        day_90_customers,

    from cohort_daily_counts
)

select

    day_0_customers,
    day_7_customers,
    day_30_customers,
    day_90_customers,
    day_0_retention,
    day_7_retention,
    day_30_retention,
    day_90_retention
from final
order by cohort_date
EOF

cat > models/marts/analytics/rpt_daily_cohorts.sql << 'EOF'
-- Daily Cohorts Retention Analysis
-- Groups customers by their first order date and tracks retention over time

with
-- Get the first order date for each customer (their cohort date)
first_orders as (
    select
        customer_id,
        date_trunc('day', ordered_at) as cohort_date
    from {{ source('orders', 'ORDERS') }}
    where customer_id is not null
    group by customer_id, date_trunc('day', ordered_at)
),

-- Get all orders with cohort date attached
orders_with_cohort as (
    select
        o.customer_id,
        date_trunc('day', o.ordered_at) as order_date,
        fo.cohort_date,
        cast(extract(epoch from (o.ordered_at - fo.cohort_date)) as int) / 86400 as days_since_cohort
    from {{ source('orders', 'ORDERS') }} o
    join first_orders fo on o.customer_id = fo.customer_id
    where o.customer_id is not null
),

-- Calculate cumulative customers for each cohort at each time bucket
cohort_customers as (
    select
        cohort_date,
        days_since_cohort,
        count(distinct customer_id) as customer_count
    from orders_with_cohort
    group by cohort_date, days_since_cohort
),

-- Get unique cohort dates and their sizes
cohort_sizes as (
    select
        cohort_date,
        count(distinct customer_id) as cohort_size
    from first_orders
    group by cohort_date
),

-- Calculate cumulative counts for each day bucket
cohort_daily_counts as (
    select
        cs.cohort_date,
        cs.cohort_size,
        coalesce(sum(case when cc.days_since_cohort = 0 then cc.customer_count else 0 end), 0) as day_0_customers,
        coalesce(sum(case when cc.days_since_cohort <= 7 then cc.customer_count else 0 end), 0) as day_7_customers,
        coalesce(sum(case when cc.days_since_cohort <= 30 then cc.customer_count else 0 end), 0) as day_30_customers,
        coalesce(sum(case when cc.days_since_cohort <= 90 then cc.customer_count else 0 end), 0) as day_90_customers
    from cohort_sizes cs
    left join cohort_customers cc on cs.cohort_date = cc.cohort_date
    group by cs.cohort_date, cs.cohort_size
),

-- Calculate retention rates
final as (
    select
        cohort_date,
        cohort_size,
        day_0_customers,
        day_7_customers,
        day_30_customers,
        day_90_customers,
        round(day_0_customers * 1.0 / nullif(cohort_size, 0), 4) as day_0_retention,
        round(day_7_customers * 1.0 / nullif(cohort_size, 0), 4) as day_7_retention,
        round(day_30_customers * 1.0 / nullif(cohort_size, 0), 4) as day_30_retention,
        round(day_90_customers * 1.0 / nullif(cohort_size, 0), 4) as day_90_retention
    from cohort_daily_counts
)

select
    cohort_date,
    cohort_size,
    day_0_customers,
    day_7_customers,
    day_30_customers,
    day_90_customers,
    day_0_retention,
    day_7_retention,
    day_30_retention,
    day_90_retention
from final
order by cohort_date
EOF

task_requirement_excerpt.text:
# Daily Order Summary

The operations team needs a daily view of order activity to plan staffing and logistics. They want to track order volume and revenue trends over time, excluding cancelled or failed orders.

## Your Task

Create a **standalone dbt project** at `/app/dbt_project` with a model called `daily_order_summary` that aggregates orders by date.

**Important**: Do NOT use the existing dbt project directories. Create a fresh dbt project from scratch.

## Database Backend

This task supports both DuckDB and Snowflake. **Run `echo $DB_TYPE` in a shell BEFORE you write any code or spawn any subagents — the live env determines which backend the verifier runs against.** Do NOT assume a default from this prose. Reference dbt projects exist at `/app/dbt_models_duckdb/` and `/app/dbt_models_snowflake/` for inspection only. Write your dbt project at `/app/dbt_project` — outputs in the reference directories are not graded.

### DuckDB
- Set `DB_TYPE=duckdb`
- Database path: `$DUCKDB_PA
[EXCERPT OMISSION]
 the `ORDERS.ORDERS` table which contains order records with columns including:
- `ORDERED_AT` - timestamp when order was placed
- `GRAND_TOTAL` - order total amount
- `STATUS` - order status (e.g., 'COMPLETED', 'SHIPPED', 'CANCELLED', 'RETURNED', 'FAILED')

## Requirements

1. Extract the date from `ORDERED_AT` timestamp
2. Exclude orders with STATUS IN ('CANCELLED', 'RETURNED', 'FAILED')
3. Group by order date and calculate:
   - Count of orders
   - Sum of revenue (rounded to 2 decimal places)
4. Sort results by order_date ascending

## Output Model

Create a model named `daily_order_summary` in schema `daily_analytics` with these columns:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| order_date | The date (not timestamp) of orders |
| order_count | Number of orders placed that day |
| total_revenue | Sum of GRAND_TOTAL, rounded to 2 decimals |

## Technical Notes

- Configure the schema in `profiles.yml`, not in `dbt_project.yml`
- The model should be materialized as a table

Build a dbt model called `rpt_daily_cohorts` that analyzes customer retention by grouping customers into cohorts based on when they first placed an order.

## Database Backend

This task supports both DuckDB and Snowflake. **Run `echo $DB_TYPE` in a shell BEFORE you write any code or spawn any subagents — the live env determines which backend the verifier runs against.** Do NOT assume a default from this prose. Both `/app/dbt_models_duckdb/` and `/app/dbt_models_snowflake/` exist on disk; the verifier only checks the project matching the live `$DB_TYPE`.

### DuckDB
- Set `DB_TYPE=duckdb`
- Database path: `$DUCKDB_PATH` (default: `/app/database/retail.duckdb`)

### Snowflake
- Set `DB_TYPE=snowflake`
- Environment variables (pre-configured):
  - `SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_USER`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE` - The clone database to use
  - `SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_ROLE` (optional)

import duckdb
conn = duckdb.connect('database/retail.duckdb')

sql = '''
WITH source_marketing AS (
    SELECT
        TRIM(CAMPAIGN_ID) AS campaign_id,
        CHANNEL_KEY,
        DATE_KEY,
        SPEND_AMOUNT,
        REVENUE_ATTRIBUTED
    FROM ANALYTICS.FACT_MARKETING_SPEND
    WHERE CAMPAIGN_ID IS NOT NULL
),

channel_totals AS (
    SELECT
        campaign_id,
        channel_key,
        SUM(spend_amount) AS total_spend_per_channel
    FROM source_marketing
    GROUP BY campaign_id, channel_key
),

primary_channels AS (
    SELECT
        campaign_id,
        channel_key,
        total_spend_per_channel
    FROM channel_totals
    WHERE (campaign_id, total_spend_per_channel) IN (
        SELECT campaign_id, MAX(total_spend_per_channel)
        FROM channel_totals
        GROUP BY campaign_id
    )
),

marketing_with_channel AS (
    SELECT
        sm.campaign_id,
        pc.channel_key,
        sm.date_key,
        sm.spend_amount,
        sm.revenue_attributed
    FROM source_marketing sm
    JOIN primary_channels pc ON sm.campaign_id = pc.campaign_id
),

campaign_cohorts AS (
    SELECT
        campaign_id,
        MIN(date_key) AS cohort_date
    FROM marketing_with_channel
    GROUP BY campaign_id
),

marketing_with_cohort AS (
    SELECT
        mwc.campaign_id,
        mwc.channel_key,
        mwc.date_key,
        mwc.spend_amount,
        mwc.revenue_attributed,
        cc.cohort_date,
        (mwc.date_key - cc.cohort_date) AS days_since_cohort
    FROM marketing_with_channel mwc
    JOIN campaign_cohorts cc ON mwc.campaign_id = cc.campaign_id
),

daily_aggregated AS (
    SELECT
        campaign_id,
        channel_key,
        date_key,
        days_since_cohort,
        COALESCE(SUM(spend_amount), 0) AS daily_spend,
        COALESCE(SUM(revenue_attributed), 0) AS daily_revenue_attributed
    FROM marketing_with_cohort
    GROUP BY campaign_id, channel_key, date_key, days_since_cohort
),

daily_cumulative AS (
    SELECT
        campaign_id,
        channel_key,
        date_key,
        days_since_cohort,
        daily_spend,
        daily_revenue_attributed,
        SUM(daily_spend) OVER (
            PARTITION BY campaign_id 
            ORDER BY days_since_cohort ASC 
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS cumulative_spend,
        SUM(daily_revenue_attributed) OVER (
            PARTITION BY campaign_id 
            ORDER BY days_since_cohort ASC 
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS cumulative_revenue
    FROM daily_aggregated
),

final_output AS (
    SELECT
        campaign_id,
        channel_key,
        CAST(date_key AS DATE) AS cohort_date,
        days_since_cohort,
        daily_spend,
        daily_revenue_attributed,
        cumulative_spend,
        cumulative_revenue,
        ROUND(
            CASE 
                WHEN cumulative_spend > 0 THEN cumulative_revenue / cumulative_spend
                ELSE 0
            END, 4
        ) AS payback_ratio,
        CASE 
            WHEN cumulative_spend > 0 THEN cumulative_revenue >= cumulative_spend
            ELSE FALSE
        END AS is_paid_back
    FROM daily_cumulative
)

SELECT
    campaign_id,
    channel_key,
    cohort_date,
    days_since_cohort,
    ROUND(daily_spend, 2) AS daily_spend,
    ROUND(daily_revenue_attributed, 2) AS daily_revenue_attributed,
    ROUND(cumulative_spend, 2) AS cumulative_spend,
    ROUND(cumulative_revenue, 2) AS cumulative_revenue,
    payback_ratio,
    is_paid_back
FROM final_output
ORDER BY campaign_id, days_since_cohort ASC;
'''

try:

except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error: {e}")

### Task: Fix CAC Payback Waterfall

You're an analytics engineer rebuilding a **CAC payback waterfall** report. The warehouse already contains a reference dbt project at `/app/dbt_transforms` with various models materialized. Marketing spend data exists in the warehouse -- find the right source table by exploring available models.

Create a dbt project at `/app/dbt_project` and implement:
- `models/marts/marketing/rpt_cac_payback_waterfall_fixed.sql`

## Database Backend

This task supports two database backends:

- **DuckDB**: Local DuckDB database at `/app/database/retail.duckdb`. The dbt project is at `/app/dbt_models_duckdb/`.
- **Snowflake**: Cloud Snowflake database. Connection details are provided via environment variables (`SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT`, `SNOWFLAKE_USER`, `SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD`, `SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE`, `SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA`, `SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE`, `SNOWFLAKE_ROLE`). The dbt project is at `/app/dbt_models_snowflake/`.

Check the `DB_TYPE` environment variable to determine which

- **Channel key handling**: Each campaign must have exactly one `channel_key` in the output. If the source data has a campaign appearing across multiple `channel_key` values, pick the `channel_key` with the highest total `spend_amount` for that campaign. Aggregate all spend and revenue across channel keys into a single campaign row before building the waterfall.

task_requirement_excerpt.text:
# Customer Geographic Analysis

Build a dbt project that analyzes customer distribution and revenue by state.

## Files

- DuckDB: `/app/dbt_project` (create project here)
- Snowflake: `/app/dbt_project` (create project here)
- Target schema: `geographic_analytics`

## Database Backend

This task supports both DuckDB and Snowflake. **Run `echo $DB_TYPE` in a shell BEFORE you write any code or spawn any subagents — the live env determines which backend the verifier runs against.** Do NOT assume a default from this prose. Both `/app/dbt_models_duckdb/` and `/app/dbt_models_snowflake/` exist on disk; the verifier only checks the project matching the live `$DB_TYPE`.

### DuckDB
- Set `DB_TYPE=duckdb`
- Database path: `$DUCKDB_PATH` (default: `/app/database/retail.duckdb`)

### Snowflake
- Set `DB_TYPE=snowflake`
- Environment variables (pre-configured):
  - `SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_USER`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE` - The clone database to use
  - `SNOWFLAKE
[EXCERPT OMISSION]
rces.yml.

### Final Model (models/marts/)

Create **fct_state_customers.sql** that:
- Uses a LEFT JOIN from customer addresses to orders on customer_id (include all states that have default shipping addresses, even those without completed orders)
- Groups by state_province
- Counts distinct customers and orders
- Sums and averages revenue (use 0 for states with no orders)
- Round monetary values to 2 decimal places
- Materialize as a table
- The result should contain approximately 51 states/territories

### Required Output Columns

The final `fct_state_customers` table must have:
- state_province
- customer_count
- order_count
- total_revenue
- avg_order_value
- revenue_per_customer
- orders_per_customer

## Validation

- No NULL values allowed in any column
- Each state should appear exactly once
- All values must be non-negative

## Guidelines

- Ensure idempotent execution (multiple runs produce same results)
- Use explicit type casts where needed
- Handle NULL values appropriately

--

with customers_base as (

    select
        customer_id,
        email,
        first_name,
        last_name,
        concat(first_name, ' ', last_name) as full_name,
        phone_primary as phone,
        customer_number as account_id,
        status,
        CREATED_AT as created_at,
        UPDATED_AT as updated_at,
        source_system_code as source_system
    from {{ ref('stg_customer__customers') }}
    -- HACK: Excluding NULL emails for now but this drops ~3% of customers
    -- Need to implement fuzzy matching on name+phone for these
    where email is not null

),

final as (

    select
        customer_id,
        email,
        first_name,
        last_name,
        full_name,
        phone,
        account_id,
        status,
        created_at,
        updated_at,
        source_system,

        -- Calculated fields
        date_diff('day', created_at, current_timestamp) as customer_age_days,

        -- Status flags
        case
            when status = 'Active' then true
            else false
        end as is_active,

        case
            when email is not null then true
            else false
        end as has_email,

        case
            when phone is not null then true
            else false
        end as has_phone

    from customers_base

)

/*
================================================================================
int_customers__lifetime_metrics

Customer Lifetime Value (CLV/LTV) calculations and derived metrics.

Methodology:
  Simple historical CLV calculation based on past purchases.
  predicted_ltv uses naive 2x multiplier (industry average for 3yr horizon).

  For more sophisticated CLV modeling, see:
  - Fader & Hardie (2005) "RFM and CLV: Using Iso-Value Curves for Customer Base Analysis"
  - The company's Data Science team is working on a proper BG/NBD model (Q2 2025)

Author: Dr. Emily Watson (Data Science)
Modified: 2024-06-15

Performance: 3 min, aggregates from fct_sales (~50M rows)
Memory: 64GB

ISSUES:
- predicted_ltv = revenue * 2 is a PLACEHOLDER. Don't use for actual forecasting.
- Cancellations reduce order count but not revenue (refunds handled separately)
- First/last order dates don't account for timezone issues
================================================================================
*/

-- TODO: Replace simple LTV with probabilistic model (BG/NBD)
-- TODO: Add customer cohort for cohort-based CLV analysis
-- TODO: Factor in customer acquisition cost for true CLV
-- FIXME: lifetime_revenue should subtract refunds
-- HACK: predicted_ltv = revenue * 2 is embarrassingly simple but "good enough" for now

with customer_sales as (
    select
        customer_id,
        min(order_date) as first_order_date,
        max(order_date) as last_order_date,
        count(distinct order_id) as total_orders,
        count(distinct case when is_cancelled = false then order_id end) as successful_orders,
        sum(case when is_cancelled = false then line_total else 0 end) as lifetime_revenue,
        sum(case when is_cancelled = false then quantity_ordered else 0 end) as total_units_purchased,
        avg(case when is_cancelled = false then line_total end) as avg_order_value,
        date_diff('day', min(order_date), max(order_date)) as customer_lifespan_days
    from {{ ref('fct_sales') }}
    where customer_id is not null
    group by customer_id
),

metrics as (
    select
        customer_id,
        first_order_date,
        last_order_date,
        total_orders,
        successful_orders,
        lifetime_revenue,
        total_units_purchased,
        round(avg_order_value, 2) as avg_order_value,
        customer_lifespan_days,
        -- Purchase frequency (orders per month)
        case
            when customer_lifespan_days > 0
            then round(successful_orders::decimal / (customer_lifespan_days::decimal / 30.0), 2)
            else 0
        end as purchase_frequency_per_month,
        -- Predicted LTV - multiplier is now configurable (see dbt_project.yml)
        -- NOTE: Still a placeholder calculation - see HACK comment above
        round(lifetime_revenue * {{ var('ltv_prediction_multiplier', 2.0) }}, 2) as predicted_ltv,
        -- Customer segment based on LTV (thresholds configurable via vars)
        case
            when lifetime_revenue >= {{ var('customer_value_vip_threshold', 10000) }} then 'VIP'
            when lifetime_revenue >= {{ var('customer_value_high_threshold', 5000) }} then 'High Value'
            when lifetime_revenue >= {{ var('customer_value_medium_threshold', 1000) }} then 'Medium Value'
            when lifetime_revenue >= 100 then 'Low Value'  -- TODO: Move to var
            else 'Minimal Value'
        end as ltv_segment
    from customer_sales
)

select * from metrics

-- =============================================================================
-- int_customers__unified.sql
-- Author: Sarah Chen
-- Created: 2023-06-15
-- Modified: 2024-08-20 - Added phone dedup logic
--
-- Unified customer view. Merges SFDC + ERP + Shopify customers.
-- Grain: 1 row per customer.
--
-- Performance: ~45 sec full refresh
-- =============================================================================

-- TODO: Add Marketo contacts once marketing provides field mapping (Q1 2025)
-- FIXME: Phone number parsing doesn't handle international formats correctly
-- See ticket DATA-892 for details

with customers_base as (

    select
        customer_id,
        email,
        first_name,
        last_name,
        concat(first_name, ' ', last_name) as full_name,
        phone_primary as phone,
        customer_number as account_id,
        status,
        CREATED_AT as created_at,
        UPDATED_AT as updated_at,
        source_system_code as source_system
    from {{ ref('stg_customer__customers') }}
    -- HACK: Excluding NULL emails for now but this drops ~3% of customers
    -- Need to implement fuzzy matching on name+phone for these
    where email is not null

),

final as (

    select
        customer_id,
        email,
        first_name,
        last_name,
        full_name,
        phone,
        account_id,
        status,
        created_at,
        updated_at,
        source_system,

        -- Calculated fields
        date_diff('day', created_at, current_timestamp) as customer_age_days,

        -- Status flags
        case
            when status = 'Active' then true
            else false
        end as is_active,

        case
            when email is not null then true
            else false
        end as has_email,

        case
            when phone is not null then true
            else false
        end as has_phone

    from customers_base

)

select * from final

/*
================================================================================
int_customers__lifetime_metrics

Customer Lifetime Value (CLV/LTV) calculations and derived metrics.

Methodology:
  Simple historical CLV calculation based on past purchases.
  predicted_ltv uses naive 2x multiplier (industry average for 3yr horizon).

  For more sophisticated CLV modeling, see:
  - Fader & Hardie (2005) "RFM and CLV: Using Iso-Value Curves for Customer Base Analysis"
  - The company's Data Science team is working on a proper BG/NBD model (Q2 2025)

Author: Dr. Emily Watson (Data Science)
Modified: 2024-06-15

Performance: 3 min, aggregates from fct_sales (~50M rows)
Memory: 64GB

ISSUES:
- predicted_ltv = revenue * 2 is a PLACEHOLDER. Don't use for actual forecasting.
- Cancellations reduce order count but not revenue (refunds handled separately)
- First/last order dates don't account for timezone issues
================================================================================
*/

-- TODO: Replace simple LTV with probabilistic model (BG/NBD)
-- TODO: Add customer cohort for cohort-based CLV analysis
-- TODO: Factor in customer acquisition cost for true CLV
-- FIXME: lifetime_revenue should subtract refunds
-- HACK: predicted_ltv = revenue * 2 is embarrassingly simple but "good enough" for now

with customer_sales as (
    select
        customer_id,
        min(order_date) as first_order_date,
        max(order_date) as last_order_date,
        count(distinct order_id) as total_orders,
        count(distinct case when is_cancelled = false then order_id end) as successful_orders,
        sum(case when is_cancelled = false then line_total else 0 end) as lifetime_revenue,
        sum(case when is_cancelled = false then quantity_ordered else 0 end) as total_units_purchased,
        avg(case when is_cancelled = false then line_total end) as avg_order_value,
        date_diff('day', min(order_date), max(order_date)) as customer_lifespan_days
    from {{ ref('fct_sales') }}
    where customer_id is not null
    group by customer_id
),

metrics as (
    select
        customer_id,
        first_order_date,
        last_order_date,
        total_orders,
        successful_orders,
        lifetime_revenue,
        total_units_purchased,
        round(avg_order_value, 2) as avg_order_value,
        customer_lifespan_days,
        -- Purchase frequency (orders per month)
        case
            when customer_lifespan_days > 0
            then round(successful_orders::decimal / (customer_lifespan_days::decimal / 30.0), 2)
            else 0
        end as purchase_frequency_per_month,
        -- Predicted LTV - multiplier is now configurable (see dbt_project.yml)
        -- NOTE: Still a placeholder calculation - see HACK comment above
        round(lifetime_revenue * {{ var('ltv_prediction_multiplier', 2.0) }}, 2) as predicted_ltv,
        -- Customer segment based on LTV (thresholds configurable via vars)
        case
            when lifetime_revenue >= {{ var('customer_value_vip_threshold', 10000) }} then 'VIP'
            when lifetime_revenue >= {{ var('customer_value_high_threshold', 5000) }} then 'High Value'
            when lifetime_revenue >= {{ var('customer_value_medium_threshold', 1000) }} then 'Medium Value'
            when lifetime_revenue >= 100 then 'Low Value'  -- TODO: Move to var
            else 'Minimal Value'
        end as ltv_segment
    from customer_sales
)

select * from metrics

task_requirement_excerpt.text:
# Customer Geographic Analysis

Build a dbt project that analyzes customer distribution and revenue by state.

## Files

- DuckDB: `/app/dbt_project` (create project here)
- Snowflake: `/app/dbt_project` (create project here)
- Target schema: `geographic_analytics`

## Database Backend

This task supports both DuckDB and Snowflake. **Run `echo $DB_TYPE` in a shell BEFORE you write any code or spawn any subagents — the live env determines which backend the verifier runs against.** Do NOT assume a default from this prose. Both `/app/dbt_models_duckdb/` and `/app/dbt_models_snowflake/` exist on disk; the verifier only checks the project matching the live `$DB_TYPE`.

### DuckDB
- Set `DB_TYPE=duckdb`
- Database path: `$DUCKDB_PATH` (default: `/app/database/retail.duckdb`)

### Snowflake
- Set `DB_TYPE=snowflake`
- Environment variables (pre-configured):
  - `SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_USER`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE` - The clone database to use
  - `SNOWFLAKE
[EXCERPT OMISSION]
rces.yml.

### Final Model (models/marts/)

Create **fct_state_customers.sql** that:
- Uses a LEFT JOIN from customer addresses to orders on customer_id (include all states that have default shipping addresses, even those without completed orders)
- Groups by state_province
- Counts distinct customers and orders
- Sums and averages revenue (use 0 for states with no orders)
- Round monetary values to 2 decimal places
- Materialize as a table
- The result should contain approximately 51 states/territories

### Required Output Columns

The final `fct_state_customers` table must have:
- state_province
- customer_count
- order_count
- total_revenue
- avg_order_value
- revenue_per_customer
- orders_per_customer

## Validation

- No NULL values allowed in any column
- Each state should appear exactly once
- All values must be non-negative

## Guidelines

- Ensure idempotent execution (multiple runs produce same results)
- Use explicit type casts where needed
- Handle NULL values appropriately

# Daily Cohorts Reporting

Build a dbt model called `rpt_daily_cohorts` that analyzes customer retention by grouping customers into cohorts based on when they first placed an order.

## Database Backend

This task supports both DuckDB and Snowflake. **Run `echo $DB_TYPE` in a shell BEFORE you write any code or spawn any subagents — the live env determines which backend the verifier runs against.** Do NOT assume a default from this prose. Both `/app/dbt_models_duckdb/` and `/app/dbt_models_snowflake/` exist on disk; the verifier only checks the project matching the live `$DB_TYPE`.

### DuckDB
- Set `DB_TYPE=duckdb`
- Database path: `$DUCKDB_PATH` (default: `/app/database/retail.duckdb`)

### Snowflake
- Set `DB_TYPE=snowflake`
- Environment variables (pre-configured):
  - `SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_USER`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE` - The clone database to use
  - `SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_ROLE` (optional)

**Note**: For Sn
[EXCERPT OMISSION]
ne order within 7 days of their cohort_date, which always includes all day_0 customers. As a result, `day_7_customers >= day_0_customers` and so on.

Explore the available staging models and their schemas to identify the relevant source data and columns.

## Data Sources

The dbt project already has staging models defined. Investigate the existing models in the project to find the appropriate orders data source. You will need to understand which columns are available and how to use them for the cohort analysis.

## Implementation Notes

- The model should be materialized as a table
- Ensure your SQL is compatible with both DuckDB and Snowflake (ANSI SQL)
- Think carefully about data types and edge cases in your calculations

## Success Criteria

1. The model compiles and runs without errors
2. Retention metrics are logically consistent
3. Each cohort date appears exactly once in the output
4. The total number of customers across all cohorts accounts for all customers in the source data

{{
    config(
        materialized='view',
        tags=['time_series', 'sales', 'monthly']
    )
}}

/*
 * Time Series: Revenue - Monthly
 * Aggregates sales revenue by monthly
 */

with sales_data as (
    select
        order_date,
        order_id,
        customer_id,
        line_total as amount,
        quantity_ordered as units,
        discount_amount
    from {{ ref('fct_sales') }}
    where order_date is not null
),

aggregated as (
    select
        date_trunc('month', order_date) as period_start,
        count(distinct order_id) as order_count,
        count(distinct customer_id) as customer_count,
        sum(amount) as total_revenue,
        sum(units) as total_units,
        sum(discount_amount) as total_discount,
        avg(amount) as avg_amount,
        current_timestamp as dbt_updated_at
    from sales_data
    group by date_trunc('month', order_date)
)

select * from aggregated
order by period_start

/*
================================================================================
 rpt_daily_cohorts.sql
 Daily Cohort Retention Analysis
 
 Groups customers into cohorts based on when they first placed an order
 and tracks retention over time (day 0, 7, 30, 90).
 
 Output columns:
   - cohort_date: The date of the customer's first order
   - cohort_size: Total number of customers in the cohort
   - day_0_customers: Customers who made a purchase on day 0 (cohort day)
   - day_7_customers: Customers who made a purchase within 7 days
   - day_30_customers: Customers who made a purchase within 30 days
   - day_90_customers: Customers who made a purchase within 90 days
   - day_0_retention: Percentage of cohort that purchased on day 0
   - day_7_retention: Percentage of cohort that purchased within 7 days
   - day_30_retention: Percentage of cohort that purchased within 30 days
   - day_90_retention: Percentage of cohort that purchased within 90 days
 
 day_N_customers uses cumulative semantics - each represents count of customers
 who made at least one purchase within N days of cohort_date (inclusive).
 
 Therefore: day_7_customers >= day_0_customers, etc.
 
 Author: Data Platform Team
 Date: 2024-12-06
================================================================================
*/

WITH customer_first_orders AS (
    -- Get each customer's first order date (cohort date)
    -- This defines when each customer "joined" the cohort
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        MIN(ordered_at) AS cohort_date
    FROM {{ ref('stg_orders__orders') }}
    WHERE
        customer_id IS NOT NULL
        AND ordered_at IS NOT NULL
        AND EXCLUDE_FROM_REPORTING = false
    GROUP BY customer_id
),

customer_orders_with_cohort AS (
    -- Join all orders with their cohort date and calculate days since cohort
    SELECT
        o.customer_id,
        o.ordered_at,
        cfo.cohort_date,
        -- Calculate days since cohort (0-indexed)
        DATEDIFF('day', cfo.cohort_date, o.ordered_at) AS days_since_cohort
    FROM {{ ref('stg_orders__orders') }} o

 rpt_daily_cohorts.sql

   - cohort_date: The date of the customer's first order

   - day_30_retention: Percentage of cohort that purchased within 30 days
   - day_90_retention: Percentage of cohort that purchased within 90 days

 day_N_customers uses cumulative semantics - each represents count of customers
 who made at least one purchase within N days of cohort_date (inclusive).

 Therefore: day_7_customers >= day_0_customers, etc.

 Author: Data Platform Team
 Date: 2024-12-06
================================================================================
*/

    -- Get each customer's first order date (cohort date)

    SELECT
        customer_id,
        MIN(ordered_at) AS cohort_date

        customer_id IS NOT NULL
        AND ordered_at IS NOT NULL
        AND EXCLUDE_FROM_REPORTING = false

    -- Join all orders with their cohort date and calculate days since cohort
    SELECT
        o.customer_id,

cohort_summary AS (
    -- Aggregate by cohort date and retention period
    SELECT
        cohort_date,

        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN days_since_cohort = 0 THEN customer_id END) AS day_0_customers,

        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN days_since_cohort <= 30 THEN customer_id END) AS day_30_customers,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN days_since_cohort <= 90 THEN customer_id END) AS day_90_customers

),

    -- Calculate retention rates (percentages)

        day_7_customers,
        day_30_customers,

)

      "keystrokes": "cat > dbt_models_duckdb/models/marts/analytics/rpt_daily_cohorts.sql << 'EOF'
/*
================================================================================
 rpt_daily_cohorts.sql
 Daily Cohort Retention Analysis
 
 Groups customers into cohorts based on when they first placed an order
 and tracks retention over time (day 0, 7, 30, 90).
 
 Output columns:
   - cohort_date: The date of the customer's first order
   - cohort_size: Total number of customers in the cohort
   - day_0_customers: Customers who made a purchase on day 0 (cohort day)
   - day_7_customers: Customers who made a purchase within 7 days
   - day_30_customers: Customers who made a purchase within 30 days
   - day_90_customers: Customers who made a purchase within 90 days
   - day_0_retention: Percentage of cohort that purchased on day 0
   - day_7_retention: Percentage of cohort that purchased within 7 days
   - day_30_retention: Percentage of cohort that purchased within 30 days
   - day_90_retention: Percentage of cohort that purchased within 90 days
 
 day_N_customers uses cumulative semantics - each represents count of customers
 who made at least one purchase within N days of cohort_date (inclusive).
 
 Therefore: day_7_customers >= day_0_customers, etc.
 
 Author: Data Platform Team
 Date: 2024-12-06
================================================================================
*/

WITH customer_first_orders AS (
    -- Get each customer's first order date (cohort date)
    -- This defines when each customer "joined" the cohort
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        MIN(ordered_at) AS cohort_date
    FROM {{ ref('stg_orders__orders') }}
    WHERE
        customer_id IS NOT NULL
        AND ordered_at IS NOT NULL
        AND EXCLUDE_FROM_REPORTING = false
    GROUP BY customer_id
),

customer_orders_with_cohort AS (
    -- Join all orders with their cohort date and calculate days since cohort
    SELECT
        o.customer_id,
        o.ordered_at,
        cfo.cohort_date,
        -- Calculate days since cohort (0-indexed)
        DATEDIFF('day', cfo.cohort_date, o.ordered_at) AS days_since_cohort
    FROM {{ ref('stg_orders__orders') }} o
    JOIN customer_first_orders cfo
        ON o.customer_id = cfo.customer_id
    WHERE
        o.customer_id IS NOT NULL
        AND o.ordered_at IS NOT NULL
        AND o.EXCLUDE_FROM_REPORTING = false
),

cohort_summary AS (
    -- Aggregate by cohort date and retention period
    SELECT
        cohort_date,
        COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS cohort_size,
        -- Count customers who made purchases within each retention window
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN days_since_cohort = 0 THEN customer_id END) AS day_0_customers,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN days_since_cohort <= 7 THEN customer_id END) AS day_7_customers,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN days_since_cohort <= 30 THEN customer_id END) AS day_30_customers,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN days_since_cohort <= 90 THEN customer_id END) AS day_90_customers
    FROM customer_orders_with_cohort
    GROUP BY cohort_date
),

final_metrics AS (
    -- Calculate retention rates (percentages)
    SELECT
        cohort_date,
        cohort_size,
        day_0_customers,
        day_7_customers,
        day_30_customers,
        day_90_customers,
        -- Calculate retention as percentages
        CASE
            WHEN cohort_size = 0 THEN 0.0
            ELSE ROUND((day_0_customers * 100.0) / cohort_size, 2)
        END AS day_0_retention,
        CASE
            WHEN cohort_size = 0 THEN 0.0
            ELSE ROUND((day_7_customers * 100.0) / cohort_size, 2)
        END AS day_7_retention,
        CASE
            WHEN cohort_size = 0 THEN 0.0
            ELSE ROUND((day_30_customers * 100.0) / cohort_size, 2)
        END AS day_30_retention,
        CASE
            WHEN cohort_size = 0 THEN 0.0
            ELSE ROUND((day_90_customers * 100.0) / cohort_size, 2)
        END AS day_90_retention
    FROM cohort_summary
)

SELECT
    cohort_date,
    cohort_size,
    day_0_customers,
    day_7_customers,
    day_30_customers,
    day_90_customers,
    day_0_retention,
    day_7_retention,
    day_30_retention,
    day_90_retention
FROM final_metrics
ORDER BY cohort_date ASC
EOF

/*
================================================================================
 rpt_daily_cohorts.sql
 Daily Cohort Retention Analysis

 Groups customers into cohorts based on when they first placed an order
 and tracks retention over time (day 0, 7, 30, 90).

 Output columns:
   - cohort_date: The date of the customer's first order
   - cohort_size: Total number of customers in the cohort
   - day_0_customers: Customers who made a purchase on day 0 (cohort day)
   - day_7_customers: Customers who made a purchase within 7 days
   - day_30_customers: Customers who made a purchase within 30 days
   - day_90_customers: Customers who made a purchase within 90 days
   - day_0_retention: Percentage of cohort that purchased on day 0
   - day_7_retention: Percentage of cohort that purchased within 7 days
   - day_30_retention: Percentage of cohort that purchased within 30 days
   - day_90_retention: Percentage of cohort that purchased within 90 days

 day_N_customers uses cumulative semantics - each represents count of customers
 who made at least one purchase within N days of cohort_date (inclusive).

 Therefore: day_7_customers >= day_0_customers, etc.

 Author: Data Platform Team
 Date: 2024-12-06
================================================================================
*/

WITH customer_first_orders AS (
    -- Get each customer's first order date (cohort date)
    -- This defines when each customer "joined" the cohort
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        MIN(ordered_at) AS cohort_date
    FROM "retail"."main"."stg_orders__orders"
    WHERE
        customer_id IS NOT NULL
        AND ordered_at IS NOT NULL
        AND EXCLUDE_FROM_REPORTING = false
    GROUP BY customer_id
),

customer_orders_with_cohort AS (
    -- Join all orders with their cohort date and calculate days since cohort
    SELECT
        o.customer_id,
        o.ordered_at,
        cfo.cohort_date,
        -- Calculate days since cohort (0-indexed)
        DATEDIFF('day', cfo.cohort_date, o.ordered_at) AS days_since_cohort
    FROM "retail"."main"."stg_orders__orders" o
    JOIN customer_first_orders cfo
        ON o.customer_id = cfo.customer_id
    WHERE
        o.customer_id IS NOT NULL
        AND o.ordered_at IS NOT NULL
        AND o.EXCLUDE_FROM_REPORTING = false
),

cohort_summary AS (
    -- Aggregate by cohort date and retention period
    SELECT
        cohort_date,
        COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS cohort_size,
        -- Count customers who made purchases within each retention window
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN days_since_cohort = 0 THEN customer_id END) AS day_0_customers,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN days_since_cohort <= 7 THEN customer_id END) AS day_7_customers,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN days_since_cohort <= 30 THEN customer_id END) AS day_30_customers,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN days_since_cohort <= 90 THEN customer_id END) AS day_90_customers
    FROM customer_orders_with_cohort
    GROUP BY cohort_date
),

final_metrics AS (
    -- Calculate retention rates (percentages)
    SELECT
        cohort_date,
        cohort_size,
        day_0_customers,
        day_7_customers,
        day_30_customers,
        day_90_customers,
        -- Calculate retention as percentages
        CASE
            WHEN cohort_size = 0 THEN 0.0
            ELSE ROUND((day_0_customers * 100.0) / cohort_size, 2)
        END AS day_0_retention,
        CASE
            WHEN cohort_size = 0 THEN 0.0
            ELSE ROUND((day_7_customers * 100.0) / cohort_size, 2)
        END AS day_7_retention,
        CASE
            WHEN cohort_size = 0 THEN 0.0
            ELSE ROUND((day_30_customers * 100.0) / cohort_size, 2)
        END AS day_30_retention,
        CASE
            WHEN cohort_size = 0 THEN 0.0
            ELSE ROUND((day_90_customers * 100.0) / cohort_size, 2)
        END AS day_90_retention
    FROM cohort_summary
)

SELECT
    cohort_date,
    cohort_size,
    day_0_customers,
    day_7_customers,
    day_30_customers,
    day_90_customers,
    day_0_retention,
    day_7_retention,
    day_30_retention,
    day_90_retention
FROM final_metrics
ORDER BY cohort_date ASC

task_requirement_excerpt.text:
# Daily Cohorts Reporting

Build a dbt model called `rpt_daily_cohorts` that analyzes customer retention by grouping customers into cohorts based on when they first placed an order.

## Database Backend

This task supports both DuckDB and Snowflake. **Run `echo $DB_TYPE` in a shell BEFORE you write any code or spawn any subagents — the live env determines which backend the verifier runs against.** Do NOT assume a default from this prose. Both `/app/dbt_models_duckdb/` and `/app/dbt_models_snowflake/` exist on disk; the verifier only checks the project matching the live `$DB_TYPE`.

### DuckDB
- Set `DB_TYPE=duckdb`
- Database path: `$DUCKDB_PATH` (default: `/app/database/retail.duckdb`)

### Snowflake
- Set `DB_TYPE=snowflake`
- Environment variables (pre-configured):
  - `SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_USER`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE` - The clone database to use
  - `SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE`
  - `SNOWFLAKE_ROLE` (optional)

**Note**: For Sn
[EXCERPT OMISSION]
ne order within 7 days of their cohort_date, which always includes all day_0 customers. As a result, `day_7_customers >= day_0_customers` and so on.

Explore the available staging models and their schemas to identify the relevant source data and columns.

## Data Sources

The dbt project already has staging models defined. Investigate the existing models in the project to find the appropriate orders data source. You will need to understand which columns are available and how to use them for the cohort analysis.

## Implementation Notes

- The model should be materialized as a table
- Ensure your SQL is compatible with both DuckDB and Snowflake (ANSI SQL)
- Think carefully about data types and edge cases in your calculations

## Success Criteria

1. The model compiles and runs without errors
2. Retention metrics are logically consistent
3. Each cohort date appears exactly once in the output
4. The total number of customers across all cohorts accounts for all customers in the source data

@author: Marketing Analytics Team (Amy Chen)

@modified: 2024-11-05 - Added conversion rate calculation

Daily aggregation of campaign metrics from all marketing channels.
Used by marketing dashboards and budget allocation models.

Performance: Full refresh 4 min, ~2M rows
Schedule: Daily at 5 AM UTC (after marketing data lands at 3 AM)

KNOWN ISSUES:
- Facebook data delayed 24hrs, so yesterday's metrics incomplete until day+2
- Google Ads attribution window = 30d, causes late conversions
- TikTok integration broken since 2024-10-15 (DATA-1892)

TODO: Add cost-per-acquisition calculation
TODO: Add ROAS (return on ad spend) metric

FIXME: conversion_rate_pct is misleading - it's click-to-conversion not impression
HACK: Using nullif to avoid div-by-zero but masks data quality issues
================================================================================
*/

with campaign_performance as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_marketing__campaign_performance') }}
    -- FIXME: Filter out test campaigns that marketing forgot to exclude
),

marketing_campaigns as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_marketing__marketing_campaigns') }}
)

select
    cp.metric_date,
    mc.campaign_name,
    mc.campaign_type,
    cp.impressions,
    cp.clicks,
    cp.conversions,
    cp.spend,
    cp.revenue,
    round(100.0 * cp.clicks / nullif(cp.impressions, 0), 2) as ctr_pct,
    round(100.0 * cp.conversions / nullif(cp.clicks, 0), 2) as conversion_rate_pct
from campaign_performance cp
left join marketing_campaigns mc on cp.campaign_id = mc.campaign_id
order by 1, 2

{#
    @author: Jennifer Martinez (Revenue Operations)
    @created: 2022-09-12
    @modified: 2024-10-03 by Ahmed Hassan

    == Promotion Profitability Analysis ==

    Tracks coupon/promo code performance to help Finance understand
    the true cost of our promotions. CFO requested this after Q2 2022
    when we realized some "successful" promos actually lost money.

    BUSINESS CONTEXT:
    - Marketing creates promos in Salesforce
    - Customers redeem via POS or web checkout
    - This model reconciles redemptions with order revenue
    - Finance uses this for monthly close + margin analysis

    == Source Data ==
    - stg_marketing__coupon_redemptions: POS/web redemption events
    - stg_orders__orders: Order totals (grand_total includes tax, excludes shipping)
    - stg_marketing__coupons: Coupon master data from SFDC

    == Known Issues ==
    1. discount_amount doesn't account for "stackable" promos - DATA-1023
       When customers use multiple codes, we double-count the discount. Finance
       hates this but fixing it requires POS changes. Estimated 8% error rate.

    2. grand_total in orders includes tax but discount_amount is pre-tax.
       We're comparing apples to oranges. Ahmed tried to fix this in Oct 2024
       but it broke month-end reconciliation so we reverted. (DATA-1567)

    3. ~5% of redemptions don't match to orders due to timing issues.
       POS sends redemption event before order completes. Usually resolves
       in T+1 but monthly reports can be off. (DATA-789)

    select
        c.customer_id,
        sum(o.grand_total) as total_spend
    from {{ ref('stg_customer__customers') }} c
    join {{ ref('stg_orders__orders') }} o on c.customer_id = o.customer_id

customer_cac as (

        cs.customer_id,
        cs.total_spend,
        (ms.total_marketing_spend / nullif(ms.total_conversions, 0)) as estimated_cac
    from customer_spend cs
    cross join marketing_spend ms
)

select
    customer_id,
    total_spend,
    estimated_cac,
    case when total_spend > 0 then estimated_cac / (total_spend / 12) else null end as months_to_payback

@author: Marketing Analytics Team (Amy Chen)

Daily aggregation of campaign metrics from all marketing channels.
Used by marketing dashboards and budget allocation models.

Performance: Full refresh 4 min, ~2M rows
Schedule: Daily at 5 AM UTC (after marketing data lands at 3 AM)

KNOWN ISSUES:
- Facebook data delayed 24hrs, so yesterday's metrics incomplete until day+2
- Google Ads attribution window = 30d, causes late conversions
- TikTok integration broken since 2024-10-15 (DATA-1892)

TODO: Add cost-per-acquisition calculation
TODO: Add ROAS (return on ad spend) metric

FIXME: conversion_rate_pct is misleading - it's click-to-conversion not impression
HACK: Using nullif to avoid div-by-zero but masks data quality issues
================================================================================
*/

with campaign_performance as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_marketing__campaign_performance') }}
    -- FIXME: Filter out test campaigns that marketing forgot to exclude
),

marketing_campaigns as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_marketing__marketing_campaigns') }}
)

select
    cp.metric_date,
    mc.campaign_name,
    mc.campaign_type,
    cp.impressions,
    cp.clicks,
    cp.conversions,
    cp.spend,
    cp.revenue,
    round(100.0 * cp.clicks / nullif(cp.impressions, 0), 2) as ctr_pct,
    round(100.0 * cp.conversions / nullif(cp.clicks, 0), 2) as conversion_rate_pct
from campaign_performance cp
left join marketing_campaigns mc on cp.campaign_id = mc.campaign_id
order by 1, 2
{{
    config(
        materialized='table',
        tags=['marketing', 'promotions', 'finance_reporting'],
        meta={
            'owner': 'revenue-ops@company.com',
            'created': '2022-09-12',
            'last_modified': '2024-10-03',
            'sla': 'T+2 (monthly close dependency)',
            'data_classification': 'internal',
            'certification_status': 'silver'
        }
    )
}}

{#
    @author: Jennifer Martinez (Revenue Operations)
    @created: 2022-09-12
    @modified: 2024-10-03 by Ahmed Hassan

    == Promotion Profitability Analysis ==

    Tracks coupon/promo code performance to help Finance understand
    the true cost of our promotions. CFO requested this after Q2 2022
    when we realized some "successful" promos actually lost money.

    BUSINESS CONTEXT:
    - Marketing creates promos in Salesforce
    - Customers redeem via POS or web checkout
    - This model reconciles redemptions with order revenue
    - Finance uses this for monthly close + margin analysis

    == Source Data ==
    - stg_marketing__coupon_redemptions: POS/web redemption events
    - stg_orders__orders: Order totals (grand_total includes tax, excludes shipping)
    - stg_marketing__coupons: Coupon master data from SFDC

    == Known Issues ==
    1. discount_amount doesn't account for "stackable" promos - DATA-1023
       When customers use multiple codes, we double-count the discount. Finance
       hates this but fixing it requires POS changes. Estimated 8% error rate.

    2. grand_total in orders includes tax but discount_amount is pre-tax.
       We're comparing apples to oranges. Ahmed tried to fix this in Oct 2024
       but it broke month-end reconciliation so we reverted. (DATA-1567)

    3. ~5% of redemptions don't match to orders due to timing issues.
       POS sends redemption event before order completes. Usually resolves
       in T+1 but monthly reports can be off. (DATA-789)

with customer_spend as (
    select
        c.customer_id,
        sum(o.grand_total) as total_spend
    from {{ ref('stg_customer__customers') }} c
    join {{ ref('stg_orders__orders') }} o on c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    group by 1
),
marketing_spend as (
    select
        sum(spend) as total_marketing_spend,
        sum(conversions) as total_conversions
    from {{ ref('stg_marketing__campaign_performance') }}
),
customer_cac as (
    select
        cs.customer_id,
        cs.total_spend,
        (ms.total_marketing_spend / nullif(ms.total_conversions, 0)) as estimated_cac
    from customer_spend cs
    cross join marketing_spend ms
)

select
    customer_id,
    total_spend,
    estimated_cac,
    case when total_spend > 0 then estimated_cac / (total_spend / 12) else null end as months_to_payback

{{
    config(
        materialized='view',
        tags=['time_series', 'sales', 'monthly']
    )
}}

/*
 * Time Series: Revenue - Monthly
 * Aggregates sales revenue by monthly
 */

with sales_data as (
    select
        order_date,
        order_id,
        customer_id,
        line_total as amount,
        quantity_ordered as units,
        discount_amount
    from {{ ref('fct_sales') }}
    where order_date is not null
),

aggregated as (
    select
        date_trunc('month', order_date) as period_start,
        count(distinct order_id) as order_count,
        count(distinct customer_id) as customer_count,
        sum(amount) as total_revenue,
        sum(units) as total_units,
        sum(discount_amount) as total_discount,
        avg(amount) as avg_amount,
        current_timestamp as dbt_updated_at
    from sales_data
    group by date_trunc('month', order_date)
)

select * from aggregated
order by period_start
